pf.license.not_this_work: Sprinkler (irrigation) repair is licensed on its own in some states, and tree work near power lines needs a line-clearance crew. Neither is lawn care here.

someone swallowed or splashed a lawn chemical

what_happens: A power line down: stay well away, keep children and pets inside, treat it as live. Call 911, then the power company. No crew is booked until the utility says it's safe.
A chemical swallowed or splashed: call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 if the person isn't breathing or can't wake up. Keep the product label at hand.
A gas smell: leave and call 911. No booking until it's safe.
A wasp or hornet nest: the crew leaves that area out. Pest control can come first.
A tree or limb on the house: call 911 if anyone is hurt; a tree service comes first, then the lawn work.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for a power line down, a poisoning or a gas smell. Yes, with the area left out, for a nest or a fallen limb in the yard.

pf.visit.proof_done: Before and after photos, and a photo of the latched gate. A spray adds the application record the state's rules require.
pf.visit.redo: Something missed: tell the business within 24 hours; the crew comes back free, usually the next day.
